intro:
The work of Scarab after the v0.1.0 research preview, done and open. Item IDs (A1, B3, ...) are stable: issues and pull
requests reference them, and they are not renumbered when items are done (done items are marked, not
deleted). Priorities:

- **P0** is needed for the research preview or blocks collaborators.
- **P1** is needed for a full reference-compatible node.
- **P2** is hardening or nice-to-have.

Each open item links to its GitHub issue, which carries its state (`status:` labels) and milestone; how items move from idea to done is in [process.md](process.md). Large items have a [design document](design/README.md), and the decisions behind them are [ADRs](adr/README.md). How each area stands today is in [compatibility.md](compatibility.md).

Linear Leios (CIP-164) is planned for the Dijkstra hard fork (L1). The design note, sources and
the observed divergences between the CIP text and the prototype are in [leios.md](leios.md).
N2 does not depend on L1 or G4; N3 needs L1 (Dijkstra decoding) and, if the testnet requires it,
G4; N4 needs N3 and a buildable reference Leios node.

sections.outro:
The O1/O5 evidence review must distinguish historical masked runs from the strict comparison
contract integrated by [#285](https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/pull/285). The former
`NonMyopic`, `SnapshotNumDelegators`, `VrfKeyHashes` and `RewardUpdate` masks were removed;
complete debug-ledger answers now require wire-byte equality and valid framing, and projection
comparisons no longer round numeric values. The [compatibility evidence](compatibility.md)
records 330/330 private same-point query answers, including 20 debug-state pairs, on runtime
`d9d089039`; later rebased CI is separate evidence. This finite observation does not establish
universal state equality or the twelve-case external candidate campaign. Operational provenance
inventory, backups and copy rehearsals remain under M11/J3.1
([#129](https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/129)).

sections.heading: Order of work (set 2026-10-29)
sections.text:
The order of the open work, with the reason for it. IDs are the roadmap IDs; the issues carry the
state and the milestone. This section is rewritten when the order changes.

**v0.2, reference-grade evidence (complete)**

The v0.2 exit gate, a Scala-forged block adopted on preprod (H1/H1a,
[#37](https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/37)/[#115](https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/115)),
was met on 2026-10-25, and `v0.2.0-alpha.1` was tagged the same day as a pre-release. The other v0.2 steps
were complete before it: executable reference coverage K2 (#49), throughput acceptance D2 (#21, PR #209),
reward pulsing D15 (#135), the sync/replay investigation D11 (#124), strict Ed25519 D7 (#26) and pool
monitoring J3c (#117); D8 (#65) closed with its one-CPU timing target accepted as a limitation. Retained
evidence includes the Preview epoch comparisons (K1), preprod sync (C4), the memory investigation (K6),
Mithril bootstrap (E1) and snapshot interoperability (E2). The dedicated campaigns D6, K4, K5, K7 and D9
left v0.2 with their acceptance criteria unchanged (owner decision, 2026-10-18, PR #184); that decision
authorizes no new public synchronization or operational change.

Release management stays open under AUD-09
([#161](https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/161)): the planned protected PR promotion `feat/*` ->
`dev` -> `main` (only same-repository `dev` may target `main`) and the planned protected `release/alpha`,
`release/beta`, `release/preprod` and `release/prod` branches, whose tag suffixes are `-alpha.N`,
`-beta.N`, `-rc.N` and no suffix. Work targets `main` until the cutover. Plain Scarab SemVer and
protected Git tags govern releases; the compatibility matrix states reference support separately. The
[release design](design/releases.md), [release PR preparation](release-pr-preparation.md) and the
[promotion cutover guide](promotion-cutover.md) record the tooling; activation, settings and platform
acceptance are owner work under #161.

**Next, in this order**

1. *Review readiness:* the threat model O1 (#74), reproducible signed releases and the SBOM O2 (#75),
   the reviewer evidence bundle O5 (#349), packaging O3 (#76), and the open audit tickets. The audit
   candidate is cut after the required readiness evidence exists.
2. *Dedicated public-chain evidence:* mainnet genesis-to-tip throughput and memory D6 (#25),
   multi-day stability K4 (#51), exact tagged-build genesis sync K5 (#52), at least 30 consecutive live
   Preview epochs K7 (#68), and a mainnet Mithril start followed by at least a week at tip D9 (#69).
   These issues stay open with their existing acceptance criteria; ordering them does not claim their
   evidence exists.
3. *Leios, built against the testnet and the reference node and refactored as the design moves*
   (owner decision, 2026-10-18): the plan is [leios.md](leios.md) 11.8 for N4
   ([#73](https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/73)), whose checklist holds the former X1 to X13:
   get the Leios team's reference node (pinned), settle the mini-protocol gating on a loopback network
   with its trace, follow the Dijkstra chain (X1, X2), the committee and certificates (X5),
   mini-protocols 18 and 19 (X8, X7), then the devnet scenario against the reference. The rules for a
   moving target: Leios integrates through `dev` and promotes to `main`, behind the era selector and the
   configuration (`ExperimentalHardForksEnabled` is the switch; a short-lived branch is for one
   disruptive change at a time, such as the eighth era in the telescope); every revision (testnet, CDDL,
   reference build) is pinned and recorded in leios.md; Leios code sits behind its own era and
   protocol-version gates so Conway and mainnet paths are untouched; codecs and Dijkstra types are
   versioned so a design change is a new version; the testnet chain from genesis is the regression. The
   protocol prerequisites are done: handshake versions G4 (#34), Ouroboros Genesis G3 (#33), the
   header intake AUD-01 (#153) and the fiber boundary G7 (#132). The Dijkstra era L1 ([#54](https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/54))
   and the Leios mempool N5 ([#79](https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/79)) follow the follower.

**Later (no milestone yet):** mainnet-pool readiness (#120, the offline cold key and a KES agent)
and an external audit, both after the audit candidate.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text:
Milestones are scope buckets named for what they hold. The version milestones v0.2 and v0.3 were
closed on 2026-10-29 with no open issue left in them; open work is in these:

- **reference-parity**: behaviour and evidence parity with the reference cardano-node: rules,
  protocols, queries, forging eras, decoder strictness, verification tooling and the hygiene that
  protects them.
- **mainnet-evidence**: public-chain evidence at scale: mainnet sync and Mithril start, continuous
  epoch comparisons, long-run stability, memory and throughput.
- **leios-dijkstra**: the next era and Leios/Peras: Dijkstra, Leios protocols, the Leios-grade mempool
  and research scaffolding.

items.title: Protocol-11 rules
items.notes: Protocol-11 rules: VRF key-hash uniqueness implemented (it was not enforced); disjoint reference inputs and unelected committee voters exercised with refusals checked against the reference's predicate failures and replayed through the Scala rules; the mempool refuses unelected voters before 11 as the reference does. `devnet.py e2e` now reaches protocol 11 itself: it reads the reference's highest version (`GetMaxMajorProtocolVersion`), walks the chain there with chained HardFork actions, and runs the version-specific checks (reference-input overlap before and from 11, VRF uniqueness from 11) from a registry (`scripts/devnet/protocolversions.py`), reporting the version each ran at; a guard fails the run when the reference supports a Conway version no registered check covers, so a newer cardano-node forces a registry review (a new era needs new builders first). Remaining: key hashes that are already shared when protocol 11 begins (the ledger counts references, we derive the set); the unelected-voter case is still in the full set only.

items.notes: Scalus deviations: the `verifyEd25519Signature` variant-A costing (patched in our wrapper) and the V3 `NewConstitution` context. items.title: A Byron address has no size limit of its own
items.notes: A Byron address has no size limit of its own: the Byron decoders (address, transaction, body) are bounded by the body (8 MiB), not 4096 bytes (mainnet block at slot 1,769,882, transaction bc61865d, an address of 7,689 bytes; `ByronLargeAddressSuite`). B30/#178 completes Alonzo/Babbage bootstrap-output checks; F7/#141 adds Shelley/Allegra/Mary, with the native network-predicate order.

items.title: Phase 2 evaluates the redeemers with `tailRecM`
items.notes: Phase 2 evaluates the redeemers with `tailRecM`, not by a recursion inside a for-comprehension; a transaction with 158 redeemers overflowed a follower's stack after a restart (preprod transaction c70243bb, block 2,216,025; `PreprodManyRedeemersSuite`, `WideTxStackSuite`). The rule and an audit of every recursion over outside data: [ADR 0011](adr/0011-stack-safety.md), [findings.md](findings.md#stack-safety-b21).

items.title: The network of a pool registration's reward account is checked only from protocol version 5
items.notes: The network of a pool registration's reward account is checked only from protocol version 5, as the reference does (`hardforkAlonzoValidatePoolAccountAddressNetID`); mainnet block at slot 4,495,760, transaction 49be5965 (`MainnetPoolNetworkSuite`). The other protocol-version gates of POOL, DELEG and UTXO were checked ([findings.md](findings.md)). `restrictPoolMetadataHash` now enforces the 32-byte metadata-hash limit from protocol 4.1, with the typed `PoolMedataHashTooBig` failure and native wire bytes (F7/#141).

items.title: Shelley's time to live is inclusive
items.notes: Shelley's time to live is inclusive (`ttl >= slot`, `ExpiredUTxO`); the exclusive upper bound starts with Allegra's validity interval (mainnet block at slot 4,498,780, transaction c7e8a043; `PreConwayRulesSuite`).

items.title: The Byron to Shelley handover writes the whole Byron UTxO to the UTxO store
items.notes: The Byron to Shelley handover writes the whole Byron UTxO to the UTxO store: the genesis placeholder is not written while the Byron ledger is current, and the block that enters Shelley empties the store first; before, no Byron entry reached the store and the first trim after the immutable tip passed the handover lost them (mainnet block at slot 4,536,140, transaction ce1c09a1 spending c1092b9c#0; `ByronHandoverUtxoSuite`).

items.title: The BLS12-381 library is blst v0.3.15 built with `-D__BLST_PORTABLE__`
items.notes: The BLS12-381 library is blst v0.3.15 built with `-D__BLST_PORTABLE__`, shipped by the `blst-native` module where blst-java loads its own, and checked at start-up. Before, the library inside blst-java used `mulx`/`adcx` unconditionally and a CPU without ADX/BMI2 (worker-a, older 2-core x86-64 CPU) killed the JVM with SIGILL at the first BLS12-381 builtin of a preprod script, with no event ([#93](https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/93)). `follow` now refuses a library that is not the portable one on a processor not shown to have ADX and BMI2 (typed `NativeLibraryError`) and computes known answers. [ADR 0012](adr/0012-portable-blst.md), `docker/blst.Dockerfile`, `BlstSuite`, `BlstCheckMain`; verified on worker-a. Open: Linux/aarch64 and macOS keep the libraries of blst-java.

items.title: The boundary that enters Allegra returns the outputs to Byron redeem
items.notes: The boundary that enters Allegra returns the outputs to Byron redeem (AVVM) addresses to the reserves (`returnRedeemAddrsToReserves`, run by the Shelley to Allegra translation before the boundary's tick); the node's boundary did not, so its reserves from epoch 236 were 318,200,635 ada below the reference's and every reward calculated from then on was short (mainnet block at slot 17,020,941, transaction 48f567e5 withdrawing the leader reward 351,635,274 of pool ffdf1b8f for epoch 235, where the node had 351,050,635; `MainnetAllegraReservesSuite` reproduces both amounts from the real inputs, `AllegraRedeemStoreSuite`). The node partitions its own set, as the function does: the block that enters Allegra fetches the stored redeem outputs into the read set (`UtxoStore.select`), and the UTxO changes of a boundary carry the block's stamp, so the deletions reach the store ([findings.md](findings.md)). Open: the era-indexed translation (`rules/Translate.shelleyToAllegra`) reads the stashed AVVM outputs, which the mirror of a node state leaves empty (`LedgerMirror.to`), so the differential harness would disagree on a chain with AVVM balances.

items.title: A snapshot of a mainnet state in Shelley was refused by the ledger-state mirror
items.notes: A snapshot of a mainnet state in Shelley was refused by the ledger-state mirror (`NetworkMismatch(expected = 1, actual = 0)`): the pool ff5181ba, registered at protocol version 2 with a reward account on network 0 (B22), stays registered past epoch 237, and no snapshot was written from the Byron to Shelley handover on, so every restart of a mainnet follower replayed from the last Byron snapshot. The reference keeps a registered pool's account as its credential only (`StakePoolState.spsAccountId`, `mkStakePoolState`; the same in `StakePoolSnapShot`) and reads it back on the node's network (`stakePoolStateToStakePoolParams`, which the pool queries use); the future parameters of a re-registration keep the network byte. The mirror now takes the credential, `normalised` of the removed `LedgerMirror` puts registered pools' accounts on the node's network (`PoolParams.registeredOn`), and `GetStakePoolParams`/`GetPoolState` answer as the reference does. No format change (`MainnetPoolNetworkSnapshotSuite` on the real registration, `PoolNetworkQuerySuite`, the mirror laws over accounts on either network; [findings.md](findings.md)). Open: the node's own state still holds the registration's network for a registered pool (nothing reads it but the mirror and the two queries, which normalise it); storing it as the reference does, at registration and adoption, is a later cleanup.

items.title: Before Babbage an address in a transaction output may be followed by bytes that belong to no address
items.notes: Before Babbage an address in a transaction output may be followed by bytes that belong to no address, and the ledger drops them: the decoder of a Shelley to Alonzo era does not check that the address used every byte (`fromCborBackwardsBothAddr`, cardano-ledger-core 1.21.0.0), the one of Babbage and Conway does. Mainnet block at slot 39,249,764 (epoch 288, Mary), transaction 369826b2: output 0 is a base address of 57 bytes with 21 bytes after it, and the node refused the block with `base address length` (`MainnetGarbageAddressSuite`, `MainnetGarbageAddressStoreSuite`). `Address.Mode` (`Backwards` below Babbage, `Rigorous` from it, by `Address.Mode.of(era)`) is threaded from `Tx.fromBlock` through `TxBody.decode` and `TxOut.decode`; the address in the set is the cropped one, as in the reference, the output keeps its own bytes, the transaction id is over the body as it came ([findings.md](findings.md)). The pointer normalisation of the same decoder is B29.

items.title: A pointer address in an output is read as the reference reads it
items.notes: A pointer address in an output is read as the reference reads it: the decoder of a protocol version below 9 normalises a pointer whose slot does not fit a Word32, or whose transaction or certificate index does not fit a Word16, to `Ptr 0 0 0` (`mkPtrNormalized`, `Credential.hs:270-285`, through `decodePtrLenient`, `Address.hs:780-788`; the natural is a Word64 that wraps) and keeps the address written again (`cAddrNormalized`, `Address.hs:470-476`, `putPtr`), and from version 9 (Conway) it refuses the address (`decodePtr`, `Address.hs:769-777`, the naturals read with at most 5 and 3 groups). The node kept the exact pointer, which the Haskell ledger state cannot hold (a Word32 and two Word16s), so the mainnet follower refused every snapshot from block 5,581,257 on (`snapshotRefused`, `ConstraintViolation(Ptr, ... (16292793057, 1011302, 20) ... ptrStake)`): transaction 9a47e091 (block 5,567,164, slot 26,366,727, epoch 258, Mary) pays 50 ada to such an address. `Address.Mode` has a third case (`Backwards` below Babbage, `Rigorous` for Babbage, `Strict` from Conway, by `Mode.of(era)`); `Ptr.read` folds the groups into a `Word64`, normalises or refuses by the mode's `Ptr.Policy`, and every pointer address is kept as the normalised pointer written again, so the UTxO, the instant stake (`ptrStake` keys `Ptr 0 0 0`), the node-to-client answers, the Plutus context and the Haskell state codec agree with the reference; `TxOut.raw` stays as received and `TxOut.ledgerSize` is its length, the `Sized` span of the reference (`decodeSized`). A refused snapshot is an Error (`snapshotRefused`) and the dashboard has a panel for it. No persisted format changes: the immutable and volatile databases are kept and the follower restarts from its snapshot at block 5,560,095 and replays ([findings.md](findings.md)). `MainnetPointerSuite`, `MainnetPointerStoreSuite`, `MainnetPointerSnapshotSuite`.

items.title: Alonzo/Babbage phase-1 collateral-count and bootstrap-output predicates
items.notes: Alonzo/Babbage phase-1 collateral-count and bootstrap-output predicates: no-redeemer collateral count using decoded set semantics, single collateral fee/stake accounting, 64-byte attribute limit and mainnet/testnet network checks, including Babbage collateral returns. Thirty-two original bodies measured against the unchanged released Haskell predicates, exact typed failures and signed LEDGER boundary controls; the output predicates retain the reference order. items.title: ChainSync pipelining depth
items.notes: ChainSync pipelining depth. The 256 timeout was not reproduced: 16 runs of 12 to 15 minutes against the public Preview relay at depths 64, 128, 200 and 256 (base build, this build, header-first on and off, and the pre-D8 scheduling on 2 CPUs) had no timeout; the upstream limits do not forbid 256 (reference client high mark 300, ChainSync ingress queue 462,000 bytes against 2 bytes per request, `shortWait` 10 s, the same as ours) and the relay answers a 256-header round in 0.26 s on average, 0.8 s at most. What was found and fixed: the receive path was quadratic (every byte read through a `Vector` of the whole buffer), 0.7 MB/s on 100 blocks of 90 KB, which on the connection shared with BlockFetch can hold ChainSync replies past the 10 s wait; 48 MB/s now. The historical batch default `--read-ahead` was **128** (64 is 6 to 10% slower, 128 to 256 are equal); the batch facade logs the round times (`chainSyncRounds`) and slow single-block fetches (`slowFetch`). Details and numbers: [performance.md](performance.md) section 7. Signature verdicts are shared with the block's own validation. Tests with tampered headers (`HeaderRulesSuite`, `InboundGovernorSuite`: the block fetch server is never asked). [#318](https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/318) replaces the legacy Praos deferrals with the shared canonical all-era header path: Byron, first Shelley and epoch-boundary envelopes are checked before body fetching, against exclusive native forecasts.
